newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine refined sugar forecast down to 2.6 mln T.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine refined sugar forecast down to 2.6 mln T.

text.p: Ukraine will produce 2.6 million tonnes of refined sugar this year compared with earlier forecasts of 2.8 million, the deputy director of the state sugar concern Ukrsukor said on Thursday.
"We are expecting 2.6 million tonnes, and farmers are saying they may decide not to plant sugar beets next year because it is not profitable to produce sugar any more," said Oleksander Bohatarenyk.
Last year Ukraine produced 3.485 million tonnes of refined sugar.
Ukraine has produced 1.83 million tonnes of refined sugar to date this crop year, compared with about 2.2 million at this time in 1995.
The Agriculture Ministry has forecast a low net beet output of 26 million tonnes against 30 million in 1995, largely as a result of drought at the beginning of the growing season.
Some of the country's 191 sugar refineries had stopped working due to fuel shortages.
Bohatarenyk said sugar was selling on the local market for 720 hryvnia ($385) a tonne compared with $450-460 a year ago, due to carry-over from last year's production.
"People at refineries and farmworkers are being paid in sugar," Bohatarenyk said.
On Thursday the Russian Foreign Trade Ministry sent an order to the government setting a quota on Ukrainian sugar imports at 1.15 million tonnes, Tass news agency reported.
"All in all this quota is higher than what we had expected," said Bohatarenyk. "At 1.15 million tonnes -- we haven't lost everything."
